plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): modelling a budget for a class excursion, calculating totals and cost per student, and interpreting the result
plan.shape: example-first: one excursion costed fully, then the class works one with different numbers, because fixed and per-person costs are new
plan.criticalFeature: share the fixed costs (like the bus) between everyone, then add the per-person costs (like entry)
decisionPoints: the choice check: bus cost per student
the hinge: cost per student for a zoo trip
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed earlier sessions? Show one budget: add the costs, compare with the money you have.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it
Cost per student = fixed costs shared + per-person costs

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Fixed or per person, a trip cost table, a mistake to fix, and the Year 6 camp.
resources.title: Budgeting an Excursion
resources.subtitle: Share the fixed costs, then add the per-person costs.

example.prompt: Is 'bus hire $500' fixed or per person?
steps: The bus costs $500 however many come.
So it is a fixed cost, shared by everyone.

example.prompt: Bus $480 for 24 students, entry $8 each. Cost per student?

items.prompt: Find the cost per student for each trip.

example.prompt: A camp for 50 costs $3 000 for the site plus $40 each for food. Total?

items.prompt: 52 students go to camp. The bus is $1 560 and activities are $85 each. What is the cost per student?
The school pays 20% of each student's cost. How much does each family pay?
Lily worked out the cost per student for a trip: bus $500 for 25 students, entry $10 each.
items.answer: Entry is per person, so don't share it. Bus: $500 divided by 25 = $20, plus $10 entry = $30 each.

items.prompt: If more students come, what happens to the cost per student?
items.explain: The fixed costs are shared by more people, so each share is smaller. Per-person costs stay the same.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Rounding the price up, a minimum number of students, and planning a full excursion, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Excursion Planner
resources.subtitle: Round up so costs are covered.

items.prompt: A $650 bus is shared by 27 students. What should each pay to cover it (to the nearest cent)?
Why should the school round up, not down?
items.answer: Rounding down would leave the bus not fully paid for.

example.prompt: Bus $600. To keep the bus under $25 each, how many must come?

items.prompt: A $720 bus. Find the bus cost per student for each class size.
What is the smallest class size that keeps the bus at $25 or less each?

steps: List fixed costs and per-person costs.
Check: is it fair and affordable?

items.prompt: Plan an excursion for your class (25 students) to a place you choose. Estimate a bus cost, entry and lunch. Find the cost per student and say whether you think it is reasonable.
items.answer: Check: fixed costs shared by 25, per-person costs added, a cost per student and a sensible judgement.

slides.notes: Session 4 of our budgeting week: today we budget a class excursion.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk; calculators are optional for checking. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with the four processes.
ASK: What is 7 205 take away 3 648?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3 557
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> regroup across the zero together on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 3 557.
Check by adding back: 3 557 plus 3 648 is 7 205.
trap: taking the smaller digit from the bigger one.
Fix: ask if the top digit is big enough, and they regroup.
notes.prep: Review of the four processes (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is 2 352 divided by 8?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 294
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> use the division bracket together, carrying remainders. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 294.
Check: 294 times 8 is 2 352. Tick it or fix it.
trap: dropping a carried remainder.
Fix: write each remainder small beside the next digit, and they redo it.

beats: ASK: What is 48 times 26?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 248
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> split 26 into 20 and 6, multiply each, then add. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 48 times 20 is 960, and 48 times 6 is 288:
1 248. Tick it or fix it.
trap: forgetting the zero when multiplying by 20.
Fix: say times 20 is times 2 then times 10, and they redo it.

beats: SAY: Now for our nine times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 9 times 3?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 27
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 threes is 30, take one 3 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 27. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 24 or 36.
Fix: 10 threes is 30, take away 3, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 9 times 11?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 99
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 9 tens, plus one more 9. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 99. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 91.
Fix: 9 tens is 90, plus one more 9, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many nines make 108?
ASK: What is 108 divided by 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> 10 nines is 90, then count on in nines. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 12. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 11.
Fix: check: 12 nines is 108, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to budget a class excursion and work out the cost for each student.
successCriteria: I can sort costs into fixed costs and per-person costs.
I can work out the cost per student for an excursion.
I can explain how the number of students changes the cost per student.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: We've budgeted for ourselves.
Today we budget a whole class excursion.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 sorting costs is reachable for everyone; SC2 cost per student is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 how class size changes it is the stretch.

slides.title: Who pays for the bus?
lines: A bus costs $600 for the day.

beats: POINT to each line.
SAY: The bus costs 600 dollars for the whole day,
whether 10 students come or 40.
ASK: If 25 students share the bus fairly, how much does each pay?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $24
SCAN boards for 24.
80%+ -> ask: What if 30 students came?
Less -> share 600 into 25 equal parts together,
4 lots of 25 is 100. Re-ask.
SAY: Each pays 24 dollars. If 30 came, each would pay 20.
Sharing a fixed cost is the first step of any excursion budget.
trap: multiplying $600 by 25.
Fix: ask whether each student pays more or less than the whole bus,
and they divide.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: a fixed cost shared fairly. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A cost that stays the same no matter how many people come.
slides.example: A $600 bus is a fixed cost: it costs $600 for 20 or 30 students.

beats: POINT to the words.
SAY: These words are fixed cost. Say them with me: fixed cost.
SAY: A fixed cost stays the same however many people come, like the bus.
A per-person cost, like an entry ticket, is paid by each person.
ASK: Is an entry ticket a fixed cost? Thumbs up for yes, down for no.
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs down: it is per person
trap: thumbs up.
Fix: ask whether 2 students pay for 2 tickets, and they decide again.

beats: MODEL sharing the bus.
SAY: The bus is a fixed cost, so I share it:
600 divided by 25 is 24 dollars each.
MODEL adding the entry.
SAY: Entry is per person, so each student pays it in full: 12 dollars.
24 plus 12 is 36 dollars per student.
ASK: Check: does 25 times 36 dollars cover the bus and all the entries?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 25 times 36 is 900,
and the bus plus 25 entries is 600 plus 300: 900.
It checks.
trap: sharing the entry too.
Fix: ask whether each student pays a whole ticket, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: What would it cost per student if 30 came?
notes.help: Write fixed and per person in two columns first.
notes.prep: Share fixed, add per person: the critical feature. SC2.

slides.title: More students, lower cost
steps: More students share the bus, so each pays less.

beats: POINT down the table.
SAY: Watch what happens as more students come.
The bus share drops: 30, then 24, then 20.
POINT to the entry column.
SAY: But the entry stays 12, because everyone pays their own ticket.
ASK: What would the cost per student be if 40 came?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $27
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 600 divided by 40 is 15, plus 12 is 27 dollars.
trap: thinking the entry also drops.
Fix: point to the entry column, and they redo it.
notes.help: Fill in the bus-each column first.
notes.prep: Class size changes the shared part only. SC3.

slides.title: Bus cost per student
slides.prompt: A $750 bus for 30 students. Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: subtracts the students from the cost

beats: SAY: Share the bus fairly between the students.
ASK: How much does each student pay for a 750 dollar bus, with 30 students?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Why can't it be C?
Less -> share 750 into 30 equal parts together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A: 750 divided by 30 is 25 dollars.
C multiplied, which gives far more than the whole bus.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: ask whether one student pays more than the whole bus, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: share the fixed cost.

slides.title: Cost per student
slides.ask: What is the cost per student?
slides.pivot: share the fixed cost, then add the per-person cost
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which cost did you share?

items.say: Fixed costs 450, shared by 30 is 15, plus 8 is 23.

say: Write the cost per student on your board.
trap: sharing the per-person cost.
Fix: ask whether each student pays it in full, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Find the total cost of each trip too.
notes.help: Write fixed and per person in two columns first.
notes.prep: Guided practice including two fixed costs and a decimal. SC2.

slides.title: The zoo trip

visual.text: Bus $700 for 28 students. Zoo entry $16 each.

slides.label: What is the cost per student?

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Share the fixed cost, then add the per-person cost.
ASK: What is the cost per student for the zoo trip?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $41
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> share 700 by 28 together, then add 16. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 700 divided by 28 is 25,
plus 16 is 41 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $25.57 (sharing $716).
Fix: ask whether each student pays a whole entry, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone sharing the entry, or multiplying, starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which costs are fixed, and which are per person?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: sharing per-person costs.
Fix: sort the costs first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: rounding up, class sizes, and planning your own trip.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: friendly numbers and a two-step frame.
notes.prep: Independent practice: sorting costs, a trip table, camp problems and a mistake. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: What will each student pay for the aquarium trip?

visual.text: A coach costs $585 and 26 students are going. Aquarium tickets are $14 per student.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What will each student pay for the aquarium trip?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
RECORD who shares the tickets or multiplies.
Their names go to tomorrow's holiday budget group.
trap: writing $22.50.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new trip with a decimal share.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner what happens to the cost per student when more students come.

notes.answer: open - listen for it goes down: the fixed cost is shared more ways
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can budget an excursion?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with $22.50 on the board matters most.
ASK: What happens to the cost per student when more students come?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: it goes down: the fixed cost is shared more ways
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: comparing holiday budgets.
